question_text: A government office has 3 divisions: Administration, Finance, and Operations in the ratio 2:3:5. If the total staff is 200, how many staff are in Finance?

hint_ladder.title: Think in Parts
hint_ladder.text: A ratio is just a way of saying 'for every 2 people in Admin, there are 3 in Finance and 5 in Operations.' So the whole office is made up of 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 equal-sized parts. Can you see how many people each part represents?

hint_ladder.title: Find One Part
hint_ladder.text: If 10 parts make up 200 people, then 1 part is simply 200 divided by 10. That gives you the value of a single part. What do you get?

hint_ladder.title: Finance Gets 3 Parts
hint_ladder.text: Finance has 3 of those parts. So once you know the value of 1 part, just multiply it by 3 to find Finance's staff count. You're almost there.

hint_ladder.title: The Final Step
hint_ladder.text: One part equals 20 people (200 / 10 = 20). Finance has 3 parts, so 3 times 20 equals 60. That's your answer.

A.text: 40 is the number for Administration, which has 2 parts. It's an easy mistake if you're rushing and grab the first division you see, but the question specifically asks for Finance, which has 3 parts.

B.text: Correct. Finance has 3 out of 10 total parts. So 3/10 of 200 is 60. You matched the right part to the right division.

C.text: 80 is the number for Operations, which has 5 parts. It's tempting to pick the biggest number, but the question is about Finance, not Operations. Always double-check which division is being asked.

D.text: 100 is half of the total. This would only be correct if Finance had 5 parts (half of 10). You might have assumed Finance was the largest division, but the ratio tells us Operations is the biggest. Let the numbers guide you, not assumptions.

next_time_rule: When a ratio question asks for a specific group, first find the total number of parts, then the value of one part, then multiply by the group's parts. Always match the part count to the group name.
deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this together. The ratio 2:3:5 tells us the staff is split into 10 equal parts (2 + 3 + 5 = 10). Since the total staff is 200, each part is worth 200 / 10 = 20 people. Finance has 3 of those parts, so Finance has 3 x 20 = 60 staff. The trick here is to resist the urge to grab the first or biggest number you see. Instead, break it down: total parts, value per part, then multiply for the group you need. A handy mental shortcut is to think of the ratio as slices of a pie. The whole pie is 200, cut into 10 slices. Each slice is 20 people. Finance gets 3 slices. That's 60.
